name: Elena Mehta
home: the blocks north of the port
life: “I still remember meeting a future banker in a night school queue.” On Wednesday, near Studio Boulevard, Elena waits by the window where the whole crossing can be seen without leaning into the road.
voice: I endowed the second scholarship only after I heard her laugh at the error.
appearance: Elena has short copper curls, a deep crease beside the mouth when smiling, and a favorite piece of clothing, a pale blue work shirt. It usually goes with a narrow brass watch set a little fast. When somebody else has the floor, Elena steadies a cup with both hands while listening.
personality: Elena often says yes too quickly out of pride in being useful. The people closest to Elena have learned to ask again the next morning, when the answer is more likely to account for sleep.
agenda: To fund a second place for an overlooked pupil.
family: Art Robles is Elena’s half-sibling. Elena decides what stays off the paper. Art brings the paper and a pen. They have helped each other make decisions that were far easier to discuss once the figures could be moved around. The decisions themselves still belong to the person asking. Asked about *The wrong bicycle*, Art says, “I gave one of those bikes to my grandson and told him it was new.”
connections: Jay Montoya. Two new contributions give the trust reason to revise the shorthand on the forms.
